entries.claim: The build-order rules contradict each other with no tie-break: 'Epics carrying the requirement IDs the PRD's MVP scope names come before the rest' and 'An epic depends only on epics before it' can't both hold when an MVP epic builds on an epic that holds no MVP IDs. The --epics check enforces only the dependency rule, so the model can meet both rules by dropping a real dependency.
entries.failure_scenario: In a PRD shaped like Toolshed's, MVP scope names LOAN-01 and LOAN-02 but no CAT- ID, and checking a tool out needs the catalog. To put MVP first, the model writes the Loans epic as E-01 with `**Depends on:** None` and the Catalog epic as E-02. That passes `lib/check.mjs --epics`, since the dependency it would have flagged was never written. Cadence then builds the Loans phase before the catalog it needs. If the model records the dependency honestly instead, the check fails and its fix can only be to delete the dependency or break MVP-first, and the text doesn't say which rule wins. This comes from locked decision D-06 (FORMAT.md says the same thing), but the step text this diff adds is where the model has to resolve it, and it gives no answer.

entries.claim: The frontmatter description now names four documents (brief, PRD, spine, epics) and then says /seldon architecture writes the document 'from those three'. The antecedent is now ambiguous, and the nearest reading (PRD, spine, epics) is wrong.
entries.failure_scenario: Someone reading the skill listing takes 'those three' to mean the last three files named, the PRD, the spine and epics.md. Section 21 reads only brief.md, prd.md and spine.md and never epics.md. Before this diff, 'those three' could only mean brief, PRD and spine.
